resources.string: NetShare-style modes create the customer network while the phone stays connected to its own WiFi, so no hotspot toggle is needed - the phone receives internet on one interface and serves customers on another. They need Location permission and Location switched ON (Android refuses to create any WiFi network otherwise). \"Automatic\" keeps a hotspot that is already beaconing, then tries the system hotspot, local-only hotspot, WiFi Direct and root hostapd - every attempt and the reason it failed is logged, and the method that actually works on this phone is tried first from then on.

Android only lets an app create a WiFi network (hotspot, local-only hotspot or WiFi Direct group) when it has location permission - and Location must also be switched on in the system settings. Without them every NetShare-style mode fails, and the debugger will report the reason.
